pairs.question: Quid est, mea Tertia? quid tristis es?
pairs.derivation: L. Paulus, noticing his little daughter Tertia sad, asks her why; she answers that Persa has died (her puppy of that name, as Cicero notes). Stripped the speech tags 'inquit' from both utterances; kept the quoted words verbatim. The question is a genuine interrogative (quid est? quid tristis es?) and the reply directly answers it. Did not include the following 'Accipio, mea filia, omen' (Paulus's reaction) nor the explanatory narration 'Erat autem mortuus catellus eo nomine', which are not part of the answering utterance.
